articles.title: Galway hurling legend Tim Sweeney dies aged 88
articles.excerpt: One of the true legends of Galway hurling, Tim Sweeney of Fohenagh, has died aged 88. ... He won back to back county championships with Fohenagh in 1959 and 1960.
articles.relevance: Contemporary local sports obituary naming Fohenagh player and confirming back-to-back county championships 1959–1960.

articles.title: Tim Sweeney (hurler)
articles.excerpt: He played hurling with his local club Fohenagh and was a member of the Galway senior inter-county team between 1949 and 1963. Club: He won back-to-back county titles with Fohenagh in 1959 and 1960. He was on the Fohenagh team which lost the 1963 county final to Turloughmore.
articles.relevance: Player biography tying Fohenagh club to 1959 and 1960 county titles (historic predecessor club, not the later amalgam).

articles.title: History – Pádraig Pearses GAA
articles.excerpt: One of the parish’s most famous sons, Fr Nicholas Murray was one player who transferred to play Senior hurling with neighbouring Fohenagh and he was a driving force in their County Senior winning campaigns in 1959 and 1960. ... In 1969 the club’s Senior hurlers defeated our neighbours and former Galway hurling kingpins, Fohenagh...
articles.relevance: Neighbouring club history identifying historic Fohenagh as 1959–1960 County Senior winners and later rival.

articles.title: Fr. Nicholas Murray RIP
articles.excerpt: He was granted special permission to play Senior hurling with Fohenagh (a neighbouring parish) winning Senior County medals at midfield in 1959 and 1960.
articles.relevance: Club obituary confirming Senior County medals with Fohenagh in 1959 and 1960.

articles.title: Pearses mourn passing of a great Galway sportsman
articles.excerpt: Later in his career, he received special permission to play senior hurling with Fohenagh, an ajoining parish, winning senior county medals playing at midfield in 1959 and 1960.
articles.relevance: Local newspaper confirmation of Fr Nicholas Murray’s senior county medals with Fohenagh in 1959 and 1960.

ina_articles.title: Draw Was Fitting Result To Thriller — Try Again
ina_articles.excerpt: Report of the County Senior Hurling Championship final at Pearse Stadium: Fohenagh and Castlegar ended level. It prints the final scores as Castlegar 1-11, Fohenagh 2-8, describing ten scores for Fohenagh against twelve for Castlegar. Fohenagh led 1-6 to 0-7 at half-time; late exchanges included a second Fohenagh goal, Castlegar’s goal, and the sides level before Padraic Nolan missed a late chance. Headline calls the draw a fitting result and says TRY AGAIN.
ina_articles.relevance: Contemporary draw-final report; exact 1959 drawn score.

ina_articles.title: Champions Baulked in Bid for 13th Hurling Title — Fohenagh Draw with Castlegar
ina_articles.excerpt: Contemporary report says Castlegar, holders of twelve county titles, were held level by Fohenagh at Pearse Stadium and that Fohenagh earned a second chance. It gives the final scores explicitly: Castlegar 1-11, Fohenagh 2-8. Fohenagh led 1-6 to 0-7 at half-time; Castlegar’s late free was wide, leaving the replay.
ina_articles.relevance: Independent contemporary draw-final report agreeing the 2-8 to 1-11 score.

ina_articles.title: “Castle” Fell in Hurling Final: Fohenagh Win at the “Post”
ina_articles.excerpt: Replay report from Kenny Memorial Park, Athenry: Fohenagh defeated Castlegar in the County Galway Senior Hurling Championship final after the drawn Pearse Stadium encounter. It describes Fohenagh’s second-half rally, Tony O’Gorman’s disputed goal, and Tim Killalea’s winning point; half-time was Castlegar 3-3 to Fohenagh 0-3, and the narrative closes with a one-point Fohenagh win.
ina_articles.relevance: Contemporary replay report; confirms replay, venue, comeback and winning margin.

ina_articles.title: Fohenagh Take First Title in Thrilling Hurling Final
ina_articles.excerpt: Replay report says Fohenagh captured the County Cup at Kenny Memorial Park, Athenry, after overcoming a 3-3 to 0-3 half-time deficit. It explicitly prints the replay final: Fohenagh 3-9, Castlegar 4-5. The report highlights Tony O’Gorman’s goal, Tim Killalea’s winning point and Johnny Molloy’s late wide free.
ina_articles.relevance: Independent contemporary replay report with explicit 3-9 to 4-5 score.

ina_articles.title: Castlegar Meet in Hurling Final
ina_articles.excerpt: County semi-final round-up from Kenny Memorial Stadium: Castlegar beat Maree 6-9 to 0-6, while Fohenagh beat Liam Mellowes 2-12 to 4-3. The report says both Fohenagh and Castlegar advanced to the County Senior Hurling Championship final.
ina_articles.relevance: Contemporary 1960 title-path report identifying the finalists and semi-final scores.

ina_articles.title: Fohenagh Retain “Nightmare” Hurling Final — Game Marred by Unruly Scenes
ina_articles.excerpt: Contemporary Pearse Stadium final report prints the score in its headline: Fohenagh 4-9, Castlegar 2-7. It says holders Fohenagh retained the senior hurling title, with Nicholas Murray prominent and Frankie Glynn scoring the goal that sealed Castlegar’s fate; Castlegar’s late pressure was repelled by Frank Madden and the Fohenagh defence.
ina_articles.relevance: Contemporary 1960 final report with explicit score, venue and title outcome.

ina_articles.title: Fohenagh Win Hurling Cup — Game got out of hand
ina_articles.excerpt: Contemporary Pearse Stadium County Cup final report says Fohenagh retained the crown over Castlegar after last year’s drawn final and replay. It prints Fohenagh 4-9 and Castlegar 2-7, describes Nicholas Murray’s outstanding midfield display, and says late points and a Jim Sweeney goal left Fohenagh clear winners.
ina_articles.relevance: Independent contemporary 1960 final report agreeing the 4-9 to 2-7 score.
